defect: The worker could wait indefinitely for source input after a pending response had become ready, failed or cancelled.
construction: Request owns one private completion signal shared with its Promise and CancellableFuture; legacy constructors keep their behavior
Promise publishes a value/error before signalling outside its delivery lock; cancellation signals after claiming local cancellation and before the potentially blocking send callback
Futures.notifyOnCompletion exposes monitor notification rather than an arbitrary user callback; native request and CompletableFuture completion wake the private writer input monitor
The consumer checks source availability and head-response terminal state under that same monitor, preventing a check/wait lost wakeup
Opaque custom Future implementations use a 10 ms bounded wait fallback; normal native requests and CompletableFuture do not poll
The end-of-input decision requires both finished production and an empty queue, so a concurrently queued final chunk is retained
No new executor/thread, payload copy or window enlargement; source reads stay on the calling thread

regression_before.fixture_boundary: Two-case predecessor fixture: CompletableFuture and opaque FutureTask success paths on unchanged base production, before native/error/cancel profiles were added.

fixture_correction: The first focused iteration passed stage/native cases and Request tests but opaque cases required TIMED_WAITING rather than WAITING as their synchronized precondition. The corrected fixture checks the exact expected state for each future type.

clean_check.tasks: Unit tests, Java 8 release compilation, JaCoCo report and all three license checks pass; integrationTest remains separate

native_gmac_async_single_session.scope: Both transports and BC/default-JCE; GMAC forced; encryption off/on with GCM; write-through off/on; actual async overwrite followed by exact readback after rejected binding candidate. This does not test safe GMAC binding.
native_gmac_async_single_session.storage: The pinned image declares only /shared; the runner overrides that path with its 64 MiB tmpfs and requests no persistent volume.

infrastructure_history: An initial modern fixture bind mount was rejected because the daemon cannot see the client workspace path; failure was before SMB and no tests ran. The reusable runner uses docker create/cp/start and exact-owner cleanup. Earlier diagnostic repeats are not added to the final 8/16 native counts.
resources: 192 MiB Gradle heap; 384 MiB test heap; one test fork; two active processors; sequential builds after process/memory checks. Modern Samba: 256 MiB, one CPU, 64 MiB shared tmpfs and loopback port only.
retained_contracts: Existing 64-request/4-MiB per-operation and four-worker session bounds
Original test deadlines and standard coverage/logging
Original sender/credit/nonce/key ownership and unsafe-GMAC-binding rejection
limits: Native GMAC coverage is single-session only; full binding key/nonce proof, Windows/ONTAP, Kerberos SMB binding and G0 remain open
The caller still owns any blocking source I/O; the worker can settle an already-terminal response while that source read remains blocked
No new qualification for never-completing responses while the source is blocked, sustained throughput or cancellation-churn memory; G5 remains open
The added Promise signal is one-shot and requires delivery without an externally held Promise lock; the Request path satisfies that contract
